text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Insurers Axa and UAP to merge through share exchange, on a basis of ten UAP shares for four Axa shares. Chairmen say merger will not mean job cuts. New company to be world's number one in asset management, number two in turnover terms, with an expected 313 billion francs turnover. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation)

-- Car makers Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen seek government's approval to cut up to 40,000 jobs through early retirement and hire some 14,000 workers, in a plan that could cost up to 30 billion francs according to newspaper "Le Canard Enchaine".
-- Credit Agricole to reshuffle its brokerage activity, after buying Indosuez. A decision is expected before end 1996.

-- Budget minister Alain Lamassoure presents National Assembly with details of 1996 budget, analysts expect 23 billion francs further spending and 13 billion francs further savings, while deficit is expected to remain unchanged.
-- Economic and Social Council sees 1997 government growth forecast of 2.3 percent as "plausible" but "fragile".
-- New unit created by Axa-UAP merger to be majority shareholder in BNP, Suez and Paribas.
-- Bigard and Alliance meat producers may consider buying Vital-Sogeviandes.
-- Cabinet meeting today looks at reform of help to entrepreneurs, designed to reduce company failures in the first five years of operations, down from the current 50 percent rate.
-- PSA and Renault seek to replace older workers, hire younger staff to gain competitiveness.
-- The European Commission opened investigations into Lagardere's takeover of state-owned defense and consumer electronics holding company Thomson SA, to see whether state aid was involved.
